structured_stats.description:
The '''Pyromancer''' is an intermediate [[Towers|tower]] that costs {{Coins|1,250}} to buy from the store. It is capable of dealing burn damage to enemies, damaging them over time even when not directly targeted. At higher levels, it can also melt defense by up to 50% of the listed value. For example, an enemy with 50% defense will have its defense decreased to 25%.

If an enemy is set alight, the flames will be applied to the enemy until the burn time runs out. There are two types of damage the '''Pyromancer''' can apply. The first is ''Normal Damage'' which is applied every 0.258 when the enemy is colliding with the '''Pyromancer's''' flame. This flame can initially only hit one enemy, though it upgrades it increases to five. This can pierce through multiple enemies. The second is ''Burn Damage'' which is applied for every second an enemy is set alight. Both damage types can damage [[Lead (Attribute)|Lead]] enemies. The '''Pyromancer''' can also detect [[Hidden (Attribute)|Hidden]] enemies at Level 1+. The '''Pyromancer''' will attack any enemy, even if the enemy is on fire, as long as it can detect it, though it will prioritize enemies that are not on fire.

The '''Pyromancer''' is best combined with other towers since it deals little damage by itself but can deal area of effect. Some enemies are immune to burn, like the [[Molten]]. This does not mean the '''Pyromancer''' cannot attack them; it only means that it cannot light them on fire.

Fire |basefirerate = [[File:Cooldown Icon.png|20px|Firerate]]0.275 |baserange = [[File:Range Icon.png|20px|Range]]9 |hidden_detection = {{Attr|Hidden|Level 0+}} |lead_detection = {{Attr|Lead|Level 0+}} |flying_detection = N/A |immune = None |footprint = 1.5 |tooltip-1 = A close range tower that sprays fire, melts defense, and burns enemies to deal damage over time. |tooltip-2 = Capable of detecting [[Hidden (Attribute)|hidden]] and [[Lead (Attribute)|lead]] enemies. }} {{QuoteContainer| {{QuoteBox|Burn multiple enemies at once and chip away defense.|Store Description}} }} ==Description== The '''Golden Pyromancer''' is a golden perk for the [[Pyromancer]], obtained from the [[Golden Crate]] for {{Coins|50,000}}, if you own the [[Pyromancer]]. Its main gimmick is its ability to burn enemies, dealing extra damage over time and later reducing the enemy [[Defense]]. If an enemy is set alight, the flames will be applied to the enemy until the burn time runs out. There are two types of damage the '''Golden Pyromancer''' can apply. The first is ''Normal Damage'' which is non-burn related. This can pierce through multiple enemies, not including [[flying]] enemies, which it is unable to damage without flying detection. Its flame can initially only hit four different enemies, but with upgrades it increases to ten enemies at once. The second is ''Burn Damage'' which is applied for every second an enemy is set alight. Both damage methods can damage [[Lead (Attribute)|Lead]] enemies. The '''Golden Pyromancer''' will attack any enemy, even if the enemy is on fire. However, if there are multiple enemies in its range, it will attack the first enemy that is not on fire. Unlike its normal counterpart, the '''Golden Pyromancer''' can detect hidden enemies from Level 0. The '''Golden Pyromancer''', in comparison to the [[Pyromancer]], has increased normal damage, burn damage and burn time, at one point having it be effectively infinite. This is considered to be an all rounder tower. ==Upgrades== {{Upgrade|Level = Level 1|Upgrade Title = Improved Handling|Cost = {{Money|325}}|Image = [[File:Common1Image.png|100px]]|Information = 0.275 > 0.175 Firerate [[File:Cooldown Icon.png|20px|Firerate]] +2 Range [[File:Range Icon.png|20px|Range]] +0.25 Hitbox Sell Price changes to {{Money|391}}}} {{Upgrade|Level = Level 2|Upgrade Title = Golden Flare|Cost = {{Money|900}}|Image = [[File:Pyro2.png|100px]]|Information = +1 Damage [[File:Damage Icon.png|20px|Damage]] +2 Max Hits Sell Price changes to {{Money|691}}}} {{Upgrade|Level = Level 3|Upgrade Title = Ring Of Fire|Cost = {{Money|2,777}}|Image = [[File:Pyro3.png|100px]]|Information = +2 Damage [[File:Damage Icon.png|20px|Damage]] +3 Burn Damage [[File:BurnIcon.png|20px|Burn Damage]] +2.5 Range [[File:Range Icon.png|20px|Range]] 4 > 7 Burn Time [[File:Cooldown Icon.png|20px|Burn Time]] +2 Max Hits 2% > 7% Defense Melting [[File:Defense.png|20px|Defense Melting]] Sell Price changes to {{Money|1,617}}}} {{Upgrade|Level = Level 4|Upgrade Title = Eternal Ember|Cost = {{Money|7,500}}|Image = [[File:Pyro4.png|100px]]|Information = +5 Damage [[File:Damage Icon.png|20px|Damage]] +7 Burn Damage [[File:BurnIcon.png|20px|Burn Damage]] 7 > 360 Burn Time [[File:Cooldown Icon.png|20px|Burn Time]] +0.25 Hitbox 7% > 10% Defense Melting [[File:Defense.png|20px|Defense Melting]] Sell Price changes to {{M

For units, they receive 1,000 damage instead. |ability1_cooldown = 10 }} {{QuoteContainer| {{QuoteBox|Now they have pyromancers?!|audio = Null&VoidN1Wave17-1.ogg|[[Dispatcher]] on Wave 17 ([[Outpost 16]])}} }} ==Description== The '''Null Pyromancer''', internally referred to as the '''Corrupted Pyromancer''', was a support enemy that appeared in [[Outpost 16]], [[Banlands]] and [[Blind Faith]] as part of the [[Null & Void Event]]. It had a decent amount of health and an above average speed. It also had the [[Freeze Immunity|Freeze]], [[Stun Immunity|Stun]] and [[Burn Immunity|Burn]] immunities, making it harder to apply effects to it. The '''Null Pyromancer''' has one ability, where it will fire out corrupted flames from its mouth. This will set any tower hit on fire, applying a 30% [[Firerate Debuff]] that increased firerate by around 42.85% and a [[Scared Debuff]] which decreased tower range by 15%. Both effects lasted 6 seconds. If it hits a unit, it will deal 1,000 damage to them with its breath. It can be spawned by the [[Null Commander]], which boosts its [[Defense]] to 50%. ==Logbook Description== "''As the Null Pyro emerged from the [[Nil Zone]]'s depths, purple sludge dripped from its gaping mouth. [[Pyromancer|Pyro]] watched with a mixture of fascination and disgust, flames burning in his eyes as a creepy grin crossed his face. The creature rose to its feet, and as it stood, [[Pyromancer|Pyro]]'s flamethrower ignited.''" ==Appearance== The '''Null Pyromancer''' is a corrupted version of the [[Pyromancer]]. It has purple skin. It wears a purple suit with black shoes, knee-pads, shoulder-pads, vest and a gas mask. It also has a few gas tanks on its back. ==Description==
The '''Damage Buff''' is a buff that increases a tower's damage, making them stronger. It is displayed on the tower itself with the icon of an arm with muscle.

==Mechanics==
'''Damage Buff''' range reduction is calculated as:
::<big>'''Damage × (1 + Damage Buff)'''</big>
:::where '''Damage Buff''' is the debuff supplied in decimal form (for example, 10% is 0.1).

The damage increased by the '''Damage Buff''' will always round down to the nearest integer. For example, a tower that deals 5 damage with a 50% '''Damage Buff''' will deal 7 damage, instead of 7.5.

Multiple towers are not fully affected by the buff. A full list of towers affected fully, partially or that are unaffected can be found below.
{{DamageBuff}}

==Description==
The '''Range Buff''' is a buff that increases a tower's range. It is shown on the tower with a blue icon of multiple waves.

==Mechanics==
'''Range Buff''' range reduction is calculated as:
::<big>'''Range × (1 + Range Buff)'''</big>
:::where '''Range Buff''' is the buff supplied in decimal form (for example, 10% is 0.1).

The range of a tower affected by the '''Range Buff''' can be in decimal form, instead of being rounded down or rounded up to the nearest interger. For example, a tower with 5 range with a 50% '''Range Buff''' will have a range of 7.5.

The following towers are either partially or fully not affected by the '''Range Buff''':
*All [[units]].
*The [[Shotgunner]], as its bullets do not extend into the increased range.
*The [[DJ Booth]] cannot have its range boosted by another [[DJ Booth]].
**Other range buff sources, like the [[Ranger]], can still apply it.
*Circling range of the [[Pursuit]] and [[Ace Pilot]].
**The radius in which towers gain hidden detection from the [[Ace Pilot]] also cannot be increased.
**These towers' attack range can still be increased.
*The sentry building range of the [[Engineer]].
*The deadzone ranges of towers like the [[Biologist]] and [[Engineer]].
**The attack range for these towers can still be increased.
*Secondary orange range of towers like the range buff range for the [[Ranger]] or the gravestone range for the [[Necromancer]].
**The main range of these towers can still be increased.
*The chain range of the [[Electroshocker]].
**The attack range can still be increased.
*The explosion radius from [[Splash Damage|Splash Damage towers]] cannot be increased.

|type = Damage Reduction

==Description==
'''Defense''' is a status value given to certain enemies and units. Enemies may spawn with this naturally, or be granted this through a litany of means.

==Mechanics==
There are two types of defense statistic. The main defense statistic is ''Percentage Defense'' which is used to calculate ''Effective Damage''.

''Percentage Defense'' is the actual defense percentage you see on an enemy or unit. However, this does not mean that if an enemy has 50% defense damage dealt towards it will be decreased 50%. In reality, the number listed is far closer to the percentage of additional health that '''Defense''' gives it.

''Effective Damage'' is the actual damage dealt towards an enemy by a tower once ''Percentage Defense'' is applied. ''Effective Damage'' is calculated by calculating

::<big>'''Original Damage ÷ (1 + Percentage Defense)'''</big>

where ''Percentage Defense'' is changed from a percentage into its equivalent decimal number (for instance, 50% would be 0.5 in decimal form). For example, a tower that deals 100 damage attacking an enemy with 50% defense would deal 67 damage as 100 ÷ (1 + 0.5) = 66.67 to two decimal places. Due to ''Effective Damage'' always being rounded up to the nearest integer, 66.67 rounds up to 67. Prior to the [[v1.1.0|Entity System Update]], ''Effective Damage'' was always rounded down to the nearest integer.

Unit defense works identically to enemy defense, reducing damage from enemy abilities and collision.

A list of certain ''Percentage Defense'' values and how much damage they actually reduce has been provided below. This is not a comprehensive list and the values may not be fully accurate due to how the game rounds up the damage, making the values occasionally lower.

===Countering Defense===
'''Defense''' can reduce the damage output of most towers significantly.

There are a couple of towers and consumables that can melt the ''Percentage Defense'' value of enemies, allowing your towers to deal more damage. A few certain towers can also ignore defense. There are two types of defense melting towers. The first has them decrease ''Total Defense'' by a certain percentage. However, if the [[Pyromancer]], which melts defense by 50%, is decreasing defense of [[Fallen Hero]], which has 50% defense, this does not mean its defense will be lowered to 0%. Instead, it is decreased by 25% defense, as which is 50% of 50% defense. The defense removal can stack, so the [[Pyromancer]] and [[Electroshocker]] can together remove 70% ''Percentage Defense'', but two [[Pyromancer]]s cannot remove 100% ''Percentage Defense''. Instead, only 50% ''Percentage Defense'' can be melted. Additionally, defense melting from burn cannot stack with other burn towers, freeze defense melting cannot stack with other freeze towers and poison defense melting cannot stack with other poison towers.

The second type has them decrease ''Total Defense'' by a flat amount. For example, the [[DJ Booth]] at maximum power can melt 25% defense. This means that when melting defense of the [[Fallen Giant]], it will will melt its defense from 60% to 35%.

Both forms of defense melting do not interfere with each other and can stack. For example, if the [[DJ Booth]] decreases the [[Vindicator (Legacy)|Vindicator]]'s defense from 100% to 75%, the [[Pyromancer]] will reduce it from 75% to 25%, which is the same decrease (50% less defense) as if [[DJ Booth]] did not affect it. Likewise, if the [[Pyromancer]] decreases the [[Vindicator (Legacy)|Vindicator]]'s defense from 100% to 50%, the [[DJ Booth]] will still be able to decrease it by 25%, from 50% to 25%.

related_pages.title: Firerate Bug
related_pages.wikitext_excerpt:
{{Removed|date = 6th of June 2026}}
{{Improve|this page and majority of tower/unit pages require updating}}
The '''Firerate Bug''', also known as the '''RoF (Rate of Fire) Bug''', was a bug that slightly increased the firerate of all towers and units. This increase was not displayed on the statistics in the game. This bug significantly affected the statistics of fast-firing towers, such as the [[Minigunner]] and [[Ace Pilot]], by significantly decreasing their DPS, whereas slow-firing towers like the [[Ranger]] or [[Sniper]] were hardly affected.

This has been fixed as of the 6th of June 2026, and all firerate statistics in the game are considered to be accurate unless affected by a different unrelated bug.

{{RightTOC}}

==Prior to 5th of June 2026==
The '''Firerate Bug''' affects all towers and units that can directly attack enemies, meaning the only towers that are not affected are the [[Farm]], [[Medic]] and the [[Firework Technician]] and the only units that are not affected are the [[Humvee]], [[Humvee 2]], [[Elf]], [[Bomber Elf (Unit)|Bomber Elf]], [[Skeleton (Unit)|Skeleton]], [[Giant Skeleton (Unit)|Giant Skeleton]] and [[Hallow Guard (Unit)|Hallow Guard]]. The '''Firerate Bug''' does not affect the firerate of some secondary attacks towers or units may perform, some damage-over-time effects applied by towers (like burn from the [[Pyromancer]]) or certain other cooldowns.

The '''Firerate Bug''' increases the firerate of a tower/unit depending on its firerate, which can vary anywhere between 0.017 and 0.032 seconds. The firerate increase affects fast firing towers the most; for example, the [[Minigunner]] at Level 4 should have a firerate of 0.09, but because of the '''Firerate Bug''', it has a firerate of about 0.117, decreasing its DPS from 166.67 to 128.20, which is a decrease of 38.47 DPS, or a loss of about 23.08 DPS. Meanwhile, slow firing towers are barely affected by it; for example, the [[Ranger]] at Level 4 should have a firerate of 8, but because of the '''Firerate Bug''', it has a firerate of about 8.025, decreasing its DPS from 156.26 to 155.76, which is a decrease of 0.30 DPS, or a loss of 0.2% DPS.

The [[Firerate Buff]] is also affected by the '''Firerate Bug''', making it less effective. For example, the Level 4 [[Minigunner]] without the '''Firerate Bug''' with a 50% firerate boost should have a firerate of 0.06, but with the '''Firerate Bug''' it has a firerate of 0.083. This means that its DPS with a 50% firerate boost is decreased from 250 to 180.72, which is a decrease of 69.28 DPS, or a loss of 27.71% DPS.

On this Wiki, the firerate statistic of all towers and units is increased by specific values based on the firerate. While technically possible to calculate by hand, due to the effort it would take, it is overall recommended to either use [[Help:Neowtext#ROFBUG|Neowtext]] or [https://fiheron.github.io/dps-calc/ an online calculator].

==Prior to the 9th of January 2023==
Prior to the 9th of January 2023, the firerate increase caused by the '''Firerate Bug''' for units was higher than it currently is. The firerate increase was generally around 0.03 seconds. For towers, the firerate increase remained at around 0.008 seconds.

On this Wiki, the firerate statistic of all towers and units after the [[V1.6.0|Violent Night Update]] and before the 9th of January 2023 is increased by 0.008 and 0.03 respectively, unless stated otherwise. This does not, however, mean the actual value is this; it can vary between towers and even between matches.

==Prior to the Violent Night Update==
Prior to the [[V1.6.0|Violent Night Update]], the firerate increase caused by the '''Firerate Bug''' for units was lower than it was before the [[V1.6.0|Violent Night Update]]. The firerate increases could be anywhere between 0.008 and 0.017 seconds, but the increase was generally around 0.008 seconds. This is the same as the current situation.

Towers need flying detection to target these enemies. ==Mechanics== '''Flying''' enemies fly above the path, which grants them multiple perks. The main immunity that it grants is requiring flying detection to target them, making it difficult for towers without said detection to damage a '''Flying''' enemy. '''Flying''' enemies have various other unique immunities that are applied, outside of flying detection: # They are completely immune to being damaged by unit collision damage, even if they would normally collide with each other. #*This includes the [[Gift Bomber]], which cannot collide with '''Flying''' enemies, despite visually passing through '''Flying''' enemies. #*Some units, like the [[Rifleman]] or [[Missile APC]], can detect flying enemies, even if they cannot collide with them. #They are able to fly over road hazards, namely the [[Trapper]]'s traps and the [[Harvester]]'s thorns (and by extension the [[Farm]]'s). #*The [[Commando]]'s missiles, can still affect them. #*The [[Barricade]] can collide with '''Flying''' enemies, but they deal unit collision damage. Therefore, '''Flying''' enemies are also immune to this. #They are immune to being knocked back by towers. This does not mean they are immune to other effects from attacks that knock back enemies. #*For example, the [[DJ Booth]] can still slow down '''Flying''' enemies, even if the purple track cannot knock them back. '''Flying''' enemies may be indirectly damaged by towers, even if they do not have flying detection. Build up chill to slow and freeze enemies in their tracks!|Store Description}} |-|Version 3 = {{QuoteBox|Chill enemies to a slow freeze!|Store Description}} |-|Version 2 = {{QuoteBox|Shoot an ice beam, freezing targets for a few seconds.|Store Description}} |-|Version 1 = {{QuoteBox|Freeze zombies temporarily with a freeze ray!|Former Store Description}} }} __TOC__ ==Description== The '''Freezer''' is a ground [[Towers|tower]] that fires an ice beam and applies chill and slow down enemies, freezing at later levels. It can be bought in the store for {{Coins|650}}. The '''Freezer''' targets a single enemy and fires a ''Frost Ray'', chilling the enemy and slowing it down. The chillness slowness effect stacks with each hit multiple times. This chillness effect also deals damage over time, chipping away the health of enemies affected by it. Starting from Level 2, it can freeze enemies. When the chillness slowness effect is higher than the max slowdown, the enemy will be frozen, which generally when targeting a single enemy takes four or five shots. Larger enemies will be frozen for a shorter amount of time than average sized enemies. Enemies with [[Freeze Immunity]] also cannot be frozen, slowed down or have their defense dropped by the '''Freezer'''. At Level 3+, the '''Freezer''' fires in bursts, with a short delay between them. Additionally, at Level 3+, it drops defense by 10% every tick. It can only decrease an enemy's defense by 33%. For example, if an enemy has 50% defense, it will be decreased by 16%. On top of this, it will also start dealing damage over time with its chill at Level 3. Additionally at Level 4, the '''Freezer''' gains the ability to throw a '''Frost Grenade''', freezing enemies within an explosion radius. The '''Freezer''' does well as an all-rounder support tower. Due to its generally low price and decent DPS, the '''Freezer''' can be a solid choice for early-game defense to mid game with very good cost efficiency. Towards late game, the '''Freezer''' is useful for stalling, defense melting and deal additional DPS through its damage over time, though its DPS is insufficient to deal with late-game waves alone. The '''Freezer''' has [[Lead (Attribute)|lead]] detection from Level 0 and [[Hidden (Attribute)|hidden]] detection from level 2.
